title.narrative: Increased capacities of employers' and workers' organizations to participate effectively in the development of social and labour policy

description.narrative: The Rwanda Labour Law of 2018 provides the legal framework for workers’ protection, covering decent working conditions such as social protection, occupational safety and health (OSH), and non-discrimination. Protection at work is further reinforced by ILO Conventions ratified by Rwanda, including all fundamental conventions and the Violence and Harassment Convention, 2019 (No. 190) ratified in November 2023. Rwanda has also adopted policies to improve working conditions, most recently the Workplace Wellness Policy in 2023, which prioritizes OSH on the labour agenda. OSH remains a lagging decent work indicator reported by the Ministry of Labour and Public Service. Beyond strengthening OSH at the establishment level, the national reporting system needs revision to align with international standards. The labour inspectorate plays a key role in enforcing the labour law. Recent reforms have increased inspector numbers, but both their capacity and quantity remain insufficient to move beyond remedial actions toward proactive promotion of decent work and prevention, especially in the informal sector. The Ministry is developing a labour inspectorate strategy to address these challenges and explore strategic linkages with other inspection mechanisms for better resource use. In this context, the Ministry has requested ILO support to develop the labour inspectorate strategy, strengthen inspector capacities, and revise OSH indicators. The ILO is also asked, with partners, to lead advisory support on implementing Convention No. 190.
